sections.name: Volume isn’t the problem. Intelligence is.

How this was measured: the study took 177 private equity firms. For each one, it listed the deals completed in the industries and sizes that firm says it targets, each with a private equity buyer and a sell-side adviser, and counted how many of those the firm saw. sections.name: A quarter broke on a finding outside the earnings work.

items.text: A quarter broke on a finding outside the earnings work.
Seventy-five letters of intent that were signed and then collapsed. Three of the reported reasons, on one scale.
A finding outside the quality-of-earnings work: a license, a contract, a compliance gap, a customer concentration
The earnings were not what was presented
The renegotiation that followed a finding

A lower-middle-market deal platform’s published study of broken letters of intent, 27 January 2026: seventy-five broken letters across eight buyer types and eight industries. These are three selected categories on a scale of 0 to 30 percent. They are not the full distribution and are not summed.
Origination and diligence are two separate events, run by different teams, months apart. By the time anyone looks properly the price is on the table and the leverage has already moved.
They are one process. The findings that normally surface in week six of exclusivity are on the record before the name reaches you, so you are pricing against them instead of renegotiating after them.
Or read the cases: Dead Deal Notes, ten public deals and why each one ended.
